---
title: "SpaxNMF"
---

`SpaxNMF` is an R package for IFU cube decomposition with regularized
non-negative matrix factorization.

::: {.hero-note}
The package fits a low-rank model that decomposes a spectral matrix into
component spectra and spatially regularized component-weight maps while
preserving non-negativity.
:::

## Model

The package factorizes the data matrix as

$$
X \approx A S
$$

where `X` is a spaxel-by-wavelength matrix, `A` contains non-negative
component weights, and `S` contains non-negative component spectra.

The loss currently implemented in `spax_nmf()` is

$$
\mathcal{L}(A, S)=
\|X-AS\|_F^2
+\lambda_S \|DS\|_F^2
+\sum_c \lambda_{A,c}\sum_{i,j} w_{ij}(A_{ic}-A_{jc})^2
+\sum_c \lambda_{C,c}\|A_{:,c}\|_1
$$

with

$$
w_{ij} = \exp\left(-\frac{d_{ij}^2}{2\sigma^2}\right),
$$

so the spatial term explicitly couples nearby spaxels and discourages noisy
salt-and-pepper component-weight maps.

## Workflow

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A["IFU cube<br/>nx × ny × nλ"] --> B["cube_to_matrix()"]
  B --> C["spaxel × wavelength matrix X"]
  C --> D["spax_nmf()"]
  D --> E["A: component-weight maps"]
  D --> F["S: component spectra"]
  D --> G["AS: reconstruction"]
  E --> H["component_map()"]
  F --> I["plot(type = 'spectra')"]
  G --> J["predict(type = 'cube') / fitted()"]
```

## Interpretation

Each spaxel spectrum is modeled as a non-negative combination of a small number
of latent spectral components. The spatial weights vary across the field, while
the component spectra are shared across all spaxels.

## Main functions

- `spax_nmf()` fits the model.
- `cube_to_matrix()` and `matrix_to_cube()` reshape IFU cubes.
- `basis()` and `coef()` provide NMF-style accessors.
- `fitted()`, `predict()`, and `residuals()` provide standard model methods.
- `plot()` and `plot_reconstruction()` provide quick diagnostics.

## Real-data scope

The package supports comparative IFU analyses in which PCA, vanilla NMF, and
spatially regularized NMF are evaluated under matched preprocessing and
visualized with a common diagnostic style.

## Installation

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("RafaelSdeSouza/SpaxNMF")
```

`torch` must be available in the local R installation.
